answer: Each agent may submit one action per epoch, but its voting weight is capped by a scarce, nontransferable stake locked before identities are registered. A newcomer must acquire and lock that stake, then wait through a challenge period in which existing participants can flag duplicate control keys. The cap means splitting one stake across many accounts adds no influence; the attacker pays capital opportunity cost and risks losing the bond if linked accounts are proven. An umber marker can help reviewers track a claim as they wander the registry, but the locked stake remains the anchor.
